$comment: Gate B DRAFT rule object for RF-DX-007 — pending, NON-EXECUTABLE. Authored only from RF Clinical Rule Specification v1.2 §8.9 and the RF-DX-007 inventory entry. Architecture-source rule: evidence_claim_ids intentionally empty per v1.2 §4.3. Expresses strong-diagnosis-anchor handling STRUCTURE only: a strong external anchor (current-episode matched, anatomically specific, sufficiently authoritative, internally coherent) may reduce unnecessary injury-IDENTITY questions ONLY. It never bypasses safety, current symptoms, external restrictions, capacity, contraindications, stage, concurrent injuries, or readiness; never silences uncertainty; never silently overrides conflicting current information (left for RF-DX-008). Does not interpret raw imaging (RF-DX-006 governs report descriptors) and does not bypass RF-SAF-006. Not approved. Not wired into any runtime.
rule_title: Strong diagnosis anchor reduces identity questions only

input_contract.$comment: Structural anchor-quality conditions taken verbatim-in-meaning from v1.2 §8.9. An anchor may reduce identity questions only when ALL conditions hold.

decision_contract.$comment: Anchor-handling structure only. A qualifying strong anchor reduces redundant identity questions only; it bypasses nothing else and resolves nothing beyond identity. No rehab authorization, no numeric values. Safety precedence preserved.

notes: Architecture normative source; MUST; permitted_use logic_with_uncertainty. Architecture refs preserved per source: V3.1-6 (diagnosis anchor quality model), V3.1-10 (known-diagnosis pathway), V3.1-22 (wire cross-object invariants). No evidence_claim_ids are cited (legitimately empty per v1.2 §4.3 — architecture rules need not invent evidence claims; [] means 'none required', not 'missing'). Per §8.9: diagnostic identity questions may be reduced ONLY when an anchor is current-episode matched, anatomically specific, sufficiently authoritative, and internally coherent; the anchor never bypasses safety, current symptoms, capacity, contraindications, stage, concurrent injuries, or readiness (V3.1 §10.3). This rule reduces redundant IDENTITY questions only; it does not authorize rehab or return-to-sport, assign confidence/probability, silence uncertainty, or silently override conflicting current information — anchor/presentation conflicts are preserved unresolved for RF-DX-008. Raw or uploaded scan images are not a diagnosis anchor (RF-DX-006 handles report descriptors; V3.1 §25), and serious structural/restriction anchors defer to RF-SAF-006. Diagnosis anchor-handling rule, not a safety rule, so safety_state_output is null and blocked_targets is empty; safety precedence preserved. No diagnostic confidence model is authored here (deferred to the later confidence objects). Draft — approval_status remains pending.
